# Churchill Downs Stakes Advance and Claiming Crown Preview: Joseph Graded Stakes-Winning Trio Leads $300,000 Dream Supreme


## Nov 07, 2026


Trainer Saffie Joseph Jr.’s graded stakes-winning trio of Haulin Ice, Indy Bay and Mystic Lake leads a compact field of six filly and mare sprinters entered in next Saturday’s 21st running of the $300,000 Dream Supreme (Listed) at Churchill Downs.


Contested at six furlongs, the Dream Supreme goes as Race 3 at 1:58 p.m. (all times Eastern). The race is one of the featured events on the 12-race card that includes the 28th Claiming Crown. First post is 1 p.m.


C2 Racing Stable, WSS Racing and Agave Racing Stable’s Haulin Ice enters the Dream Supreme following a third-place effort in the $150,000 Liberty Bell on Sept. 19 at Parx. In her previous start, Haulin Ice finished second to Maida in the $250,000 Honorable Miss (GII) at Saratoga. The 5-year-old daughter of Coal Front holds the record for most earnings by an Arkansas-bred of $1,307,300. Francisco Arrieta, who rode Haulin Ice to back-to-back wins in the $250,000 Matron at Oaklawn Park, has the mount from post No. 2.


Agave Racing Stable and Miller Racing’s Indy Bay will make her Churchill Downs debut with Jose Ortiz aboard from post 5. The 4-year-old daughter of Take Charge Indy won last year’s $750,000 Charles Town Oaks (GII) and $150,000 Jersey Girl at Saratoga.


Miller Racing, BAG Racing Stables and Stefania Farms’ Mystic Lake finished second to Maida in the $200,000 Endine on Oct. 17 at Delaware Park. The 5-year-old daughter of Mo Town won the $750,000 Charles Town Oaks (GII) in 2024 and $215,000 Inside Information (GII) last year. She has won 13 of 28 starts and earned $1,704,102. Tyler Gaffalione has the mount and drew the rail.


The complete field for the Dream Supreme from the rail out (with jockey and trainer):


Mystic Lake (Gaffalione, Joseph)
Haulin Ice (Arrieta, Joseph)
A.Z. Wildcat (Florent Geroux, John Sadler)
Echo Sound (Luis Saez, Rusty Arnold II)
Indy Bay (Ortiz, Joseph)
Justinqueso (Brian Hernandez Jr., Ian Wilkes)
CLAIMING CROWN FEATURES TOP BLUE COLLAR HORSES FROM ACROSS NORTH AMERICA – Some of North America’s top blue-collar horses will converge at Churchill Downs next Saturday for the 28th Claiming Crown, which features nine supercharged starter allowance races worth a combined $1.2 million in purses.


First post is 1 p.m. for the 12-race card, which also includes the $300,000 Dream Supreme (Listed). The Claiming Crown begins in Race 4 at 2:28 p.m.


Inaugurated in 1999, the National Horsemen’s Benevolent and Protective Association and Thoroughbred Owners and Breeders Association chose to bring back the Claiming Crown to Louisville for a fourth time and third year in a row.


Horseplayers responded to last year’s Claiming Crown at Churchill Downs with $12.8 million in wagers on the program.


One of the headliners this year is Morris Kernan Jr. and Jagger Inc.’s Kerness K, who will seek his 12th straight victory when he faces nine rivals in the $100,000 Ready’s Rocket Express. The 4-year-old gelding, who trainer Jamie Ness claimed back for $7,500 in March, leads all North American Thoroughbreds in wins this year, 11-10 over Hurricane Lassie.
